Candle: Which candle is it?
Candle. The board has 10x10 sites (160x160 cells). The window shows one site; each move goes to the next site (up, down, left or right). One large candle in a holder stands on a plain pink board. Four parts sit in their places, each drawn as one big black shape filling one site (a part that sits at two or more sites shows the same shape at each of them): its flame at the top: a black eight-point star or a black square; two wax drips side by side in the middle: a black ring or a black diamond; the two holder handles at the far left and far right: a black V shape or a black disc; the two holder feet at the bottom: a black triangle pointing up or a wide flat black bar. Every other site shows plain pink. The whole candle may sit one site higher, lower, left or right, or one site diagonally. Question: Which candle is it? The answer is one of eight candles, each with its own parts: boreas = a black eight-point star, a black ring, a black V shape, a black triangle pointing up; eurus = a black eight-point star, a black ring, a black disc, a wide flat black bar; notus = a black eight-point star, a black diamond, a black V shape, a wide flat black bar; zephyr = a black eight-point star, a black diamond, a black disc, a black triangle pointing up; sirocco = a black square, a black ring, a black V shape, a wide flat black bar; mistral = a black square, a black ring, a black disc, a black triangle pointing up; chinook = a black square, a black diamond, a black V shape, a black triangle pointing up; foehn = a black square, a black diamond, a black disc, a wide flat black bar. Answer with its name. You may answer at any time; you do not need to see every site. Score: 20 if the answer is right, minus 10, minus 0.1 per move (movement budget 35).
The answers: 1 = boreas, 2 = eurus, 3 = notus, 4 = zephyr, 5 = sirocco, 6 = mistral, 7 = chinook, 8 = foehn.
